Title: Freeze challenge, scope and cut list
scope: Approve one five-day, two-actions/day lunar mission; five resources and three challenge events, with a guaranteed smaller fallback if behind schedule.
acceptance: One-page scope freezes objectives, target age 7–12 and explicit non-goals
Must-have vs optional features distinguished
All three owners acknowledge rules before coding
verification: Check scope against the 2026 challenge brief; record any uncertainties.

Title: NASA science and evidence map
scope: Confirm DONKI FLR/SEP as a challenge-listed resource, identify legitimate NASA example event(s), source URLs, usage terms, caveats and citation format. RadLab and CSA are background context, not lunar dose calculators.
acceptance: A NASA challenge-listed source URL and API docs recorded
Event fields and source URLs specified; no invented NASA readings
Clearly separate NASA observations, model assumptions and educational explanations
Record fallback provenance method
verification: Independent source-link check; one concrete event record identified before integrating.

Title: Freeze simulation rules and balanced scenarios
scope: Freeze 0–100 game-unit values for oxygen/power/water/food/radiationRisk, action costs, 2 actions/day, event timing, daily drain, failure/success. Document numbers as game assumptions.
acceptance: Action effects deterministic and bounded
Event applied before daily decisions; daily drain after two actions or finish-day
Success after day 5; fail when life resource reaches 0 or risk reaches 100
No physically claimed mission rates
Example success and failure walkthroughs
verification: Manually replay two representative five-day paths and inspect for trivial infinite resource exploits.

Title: Freeze distinctive UI storyboard and interaction map
scope: Approve cinematic landing, isometric/clickable lunar base, 4 hotspots, game HUD, event drawer, NASA learn panel and results. Avoid generic SaaS-dashboard visuals.
acceptance: Four-screen flow agreed
Each hotspot has accessible label and action panel
Readable mobile fallback is included
All images/original SVG plans avoid generated NASA branding
verification: Walk through Start -> select module -> choose action -> event -> result.

Title: Freeze GitHub workflow and NASA submission checklist
scope: Lock repository/board naming, owner-to-reviewer matrix, task IDs, GitHub branch policy, issue gates, live pitch/submission checklist; verify team registration.
acceptance: No project work starts before authorized 9am Nov 14
Issue IDs stable TRI-001..TRI-031
Every issue shows responsible name and dependency
Public demo, NASA citation, AI disclosure, 5-minute pitch and project-page requirements recorded
verification: Cross-check user-supplied local judging documents and NASA site.

Title: 9am repo, board, Next.js scaffold and branch setup
File boundaries: package.json; src/app/; tsconfig.json; next.config.*; README.md; .gitignore; docs/
scope: At/after 9:00 AM local hackathon start, Abhinaya creates the one GitHub repository, Next.js scaffold, main/develop branches and issue board; publishes scaffold immediately so other members can clone. Import task issues in parallel or immediately after bootstrap; a Projects board permissions issue must never block coding.
acceptance: One verified repository exists under Abhinaya or another expressly agreed owner; no duplicate GitHub repo
main and develop exist and scaffold is pushed so team can clone
npm run build succeeds on the initial scaffold
GitHub issue importer creates or confirms all 31 TRI IDs without duplicates; board may be added later if permissions delay
Actual GitHub handles verified and invites sent; no guessed assignees
verification: npm run build; gh issue list; gh project item-list or board UI; git status.

Title: Create shared interfaces and mock fixture contracts
scope: Create canonical TypeScript types, pure function signatures, event schema, bounded resource helpers and small typed mock data. Notify both consumers before they code.
acceptance: One GameState/Action/Scenario type defined
NASA normalized event type defined
No duplicate state types in UI or routes
Exports resolve in both server and client contexts
verification: npm run build; typecheck if available; share commit SHA in task.

Title: Pure resource simulation engine
scope: Implement immutable deterministic applyAction, nextDay/finishDay, bounds, consumptions, event side effects as separate pure functions. No React dependency.
acceptance: Two-actions/day enforced
An action has meaningful trade-offs
No NaN, negative values, or overflow
Function results are reproducible
Game units are clearly educational assumptions
verification: Automated action/bounds/invalid action tests; run twice for reproducibility.

Title: Five-day progression, score and outcomes
scope: Implement event-before-decisions daily phases, success/failure rules, score summary, history and restartable initial state.
acceptance: Exactly five days when surviving
Success and loss states reachable
Score uses visible deterministic rules
New mission resets everything
History records decisions and NASA scenario reference
verification: Unit tests for day boundary, 0 oxygen, radiation risk 100 and successful 5-day mission.

Title: NASA DONKI backend route, normalization and safe fallback
scope: Implement standalone server-side NASA DONKI ingestion as GET /api/nasa/events, with input validation, bounded requests/timeouts, source/provenance metadata, and a verified bundled historical-record fallback. Work from frozen docs/INTERFACES.md response shape; do not depend on shared GameState engine code. Keep server-only NASA_API_KEY out of client bundles.
acceptance: Real endpoint works when NASA responds
Missing key uses safe demo/fallback behavior; no key leaks
Offline/bad-response branch loads only traceable, verified stored record
Normalized id/type/date/sourceUrl exposed
Timeout/error handled without crashing the game
No false lunar dose inference
verification: Test success with curated verified source, provider-failure fallback, provenance and no secret in response.

Title: Three concise mission events and consequences
scope: Author 3 self-contained scenario data records in JSON from frozen GAME_RULES/INTERFACES docs: solar activity using source-identified NASA DONKI record and two explicitly fictional emergencies. Include 2+ real resource-trade-off choices each. Do not require Vibhushan game code or touch canonical GameState.
acceptance: 3 events have unique ID and distinct choices
NASA event carries citation and date
Non-NASA scenarios labeled educational simulations
Each choice has resource trade-off and short learning explanation
No scientific claims beyond cited facts
verification: Test event IDs, choice effects, provenance and no broken references.

Title: Design tokens and reusable game shell
scope: Build original lunar visual foundation: dark navy, cyan, amber, scientific legibility; responsive page shell, typography, reusable buttons and panels, but not generic component dashboard.
acceptance: Unified tokens and accessible contrast
Desktop 1366x768 and mobile 390x844 legible
No NASA logo; decorative assets original or properly credited
Screens use same underlying design
verification: Manually inspect responsive widths, focus styles and npm run build.

Title: Landing screen and 30-second tutorial
scope: Create cinematic introduction showing Moon base, one-sentence mission, three astronauts, 5-day goal and simple Start Mission; optional one-screen tutorial overlay.
acceptance: One-click entry to real mission
Readable purpose and core controls
Keyboard access to Start
No dead or fake controls
verification: Start -> tutorial -> game works on desktop and mobile.

Title: Original clickable lunar base SVG scene
scope: Draw a performant 2.5D lunar base via original inline SVG/CSS with four distinctly clickable modules: life support, solar arrays, greenhouse, radiation shelter. Include labels/hotspots and selected-module feedback.
acceptance: 4 modules keyboard/click/tap reachable
Selected module visually highlighted
Looks like game environment, not card grid
Works at mobile and desktop widths
No external NASA branding or inaccessible icons
verification: Manual hotspot, keyboard and touch test; no horizontal overflow.

Title: Mission HUD: day, status, resources
scope: Build a mission HUD with resource meters, mission day, actions remaining, mission state and warning thresholds. It accepts display props and typed callbacks; use local display-only fixture props, not imports from unfinished engine modules. Do not implement competing simulation logic.
acceptance: Displays supplied resource/day/action values, never embeds fixed sample values inside production HUD component
High radiation risk is visually distinct from healthy resources
Accessible numeric labels, warnings and focus behavior
Works with display-only fixtures for 0, 100 and warning-threshold extremes
verification: Render mock starting/low-resource/end states; typecheck.

Title: Bind building interactions to engine actions
scope: Integrate Abhinaya’s stable lunar UI/hotspots and mission HUD with Vibhushan’s canonical simulation engine via explicit callbacks and derived view props. Replace all UI-only fixtures. Coordinate changes to UI-owned integration pages after Abhinaya’s PR is reviewed; never overwrite her work.
acceptance: Every action updates exactly via engine
Cannot exceed actions/day
Disabled actions explain why
HUD and controls stay synchronized
No duplicated simulation algorithm in components
verification: Actual gameplay: click each module, trigger valid action, watch resources and day state update; verify action budget and failure behavior.

Title: Mission event modal and choice consequences UX
scope: Implement a standalone scenario modal with choice buttons and sourced/caveated explanation, accepting scenario/view data and onSelect callback. Can be developed with local fixture data and must not reach into unfinished HUD or shared GameState.
acceptance: Event displayed before choices
Player must resolve event before moving on
NASA event has source link/date
Choice updates engine or emits typed callback
Modal dismiss and keyboard behavior safe
verification: Render with fixture; verify 2+ decision options, keyboard activation and source/caveat display.

Title: NASA science facts panel and attribution
scope: Create standalone NASA-learning panel accepting verified citation data, short factual science explanations and an explicit game-assumption caveat. Avoid dependency on Abhinaya style tokens; use component-local accessible styling and coordinate visuals during integration.
acceptance: NASA evidence linked to actual behavior
Each fact includes valid URL
No invented Moon radiation dose claim
References accessible during demo
Text understandable to 7–12 audience
verification: Click NASA explanation and verify references in private browser.

Title: Mission results, success/failure and replay
scope: Create standalone mission results/replay UI using simple display props: win/loss, game score, remaining resource summary, one lesson learned and replay callback. It must not implement scoring math; simulation owner connects actual values at integration.
acceptance: Success and failure views differ clearly
Results use supplied outcome, resource summary and score props with no local scoring algorithm
Replay button emits the callback; parent reset occurs later at integration
No unimplemented buttons or fictional NASA statistics
verification: Render success/failure fixture cases and replay callback manually or with component tests.

Title: End-to-end integration into develop and stable main
scope: On integration branch, combine the three reviewed workstream PRs with one tested single-player end-to-end mission. Wire NASA data route, bundled fallback, scenario choice dialog, HUD, explanations, results and replay. Record real tests; publish stable demo only when working. Do not block workstream development on the GitHub Projects board.
acceptance: Start -> 5-day decisions -> 3 events -> results -> replay works
Live API and fallback paths work
No TypeScript/build or fatal console errors
Main contains known-good demo build and can run offline
All source links open
verification: npm run build, npm run dev; manually prove success, failure, fallback, mobile and fresh-clone installation.

Title: Smoke tests, regression and failure cases
scope: Independently execute complete playable smoke and failure cases on the integrated build: success, failure, event decision, input bounds, keyboard/touch basics, offline NASA fallback, and source links. Report reproducible findings; do not silently modify another owner’s module.
acceptance: Key engine functions covered
NASA route fallback verified
At least one win and one loss scenario tested
No severe crash or blocked interaction
Any known minor limitations documented
verification: Evidence checklist with actual commands and screenshots/logs; report PASS/FAIL and retest after fixes.

Title: Responsive + keyboard accessibility fix pass
scope: Polish accessible keyboard/touch behavior and responsive layout of Abhinaya-owned UI without waiting for final engine integration. Do not refactor others’ science or game engine files.
acceptance: Desktop and mobile playable
Clear focus ring and labels
No clipped event dialog
No major text contrast issue
verification: Manual screen-size and keyboard smoke tests.

Title: Motion and visual polish within strict budget
scope: Add a few purposeful CSS/Motion transitions to chosen hotspots, gauges and event alert; disable or reduce for reduced motion.
acceptance: No layout jumps or stutter
prefers-reduced-motion respected
No broken UI or additional heavy packages
verification: Manual reduced-motion and low-end browser test.

Title: Optional local saved progress
scope: Persist progress only to browser localStorage with versioned schema and safe recovery; implement only if everything else is ready.
acceptance: Resume works
Invalid save resets safely
No personal information collected
verification: Reload and corrupt-data test.

Title: Science, references and AI/license audit
scope: Independently audit NASA source URLs, verified historical DONKI record, the distinction between space-weather observation and lunar dose, educational simulation assumptions, AI/SI use, external asset/code licenses, and attribution in code/README; final cross-check again after integration.
acceptance: At least one challenge-listed NASA source actually affects the app
Measurements vs educational model distinguished
All borrowed source material licensed and credited
AI-tool roles accurately disclosed
All links work
verification: Review README, ScienceDrawer and APIs against raw citations.

Title: Produce 30-second subtitled demo OR max-seven slides
scope: Create the agreed six-slide online submission deck as a public view-only Google Slides or exported slide PDF, using real tested application screenshots and source citations. This is the sole online demo artifact; a 30-second subtitled video is an acceptable backup alternative, not an additional required deliverable. Keep within seven slides total, including any title slide.
acceptance: Exactly one demo format chosen
Video <=30 sec and English subtitles OR <=7 slides counting title
Link opens in incognito, no login
Shows actual built features, not mockups
verification: Inspect full demo playback or count slides; incognito link test.

Title: Complete README, project description and links
scope: Prepare a readable README, accurate science source list, installation/run instructions, source acknowledgment and project summary. Start while other members build using confirmed architecture; update screenshots and final tested status after integration rather than claiming unfinished work is complete.
acceptance: Fresh-clone run commands verified
50–200-word high-level summary
Includes source/API/AI disclosure and link placeholders
No unimplemented feature claimed
verification: Run README commands from clean environment; count summary words.

Title: Rehearse virtual 5-minute pitch and Q&A
scope: Prepare and rehearse the five-minute virtual pitch script/storyboard with the working UI prototype, leaving labeled placeholders for real NASA data outcome and end-to-end demo until integration is confirmed. Final pitch rehearsal must use the tested integrated version.
acceptance: Live demo timed under 5 min
Shows NASA-based event, consequences, educational outcome
Answers science approximation, no backend DB, project originality
Meeting link/slot verified with organizer
verification: Time one complete dry run and recover from simulated API outage.

Title: Complete NASA project page and verify submission
scope: Submit project through actual TriOrbit NASA team page; fill all required fields and confirm successful submission before official deadline.
acceptance: Name, 50–200 summary, project detail, public demo and repo links entered
NASA sources and all other credits listed
AI/SI disclosed as instructed
Final save and submitted state verified, screenshot receipt recorded
verification: Second-person review, incognito link test, confirm published/submitted status.

Title: Optional Vercel deployment
scope: Deploy only once local demo and QA are stable; configure server API key only in secret Vercel environment, verify fallback and public access.
acceptance: Production build works
No exposed API key
Public URL works incognito
verification: npm run build; live end-to-end test.

Title: Optional expanded replay insights/scenarios
scope: Add variant mission/replay learnings only after submission requirements are complete; do not add unsupported science claims.
acceptance: Does not break original 5-day mission
Science and scoring still deterministic
Replay clearly compares choices
verification: Regression test and verify old mission unchanged.
